items.Sentence: The tertiary wastewater treatment process prior to discharge from Discharge Point 001 includes a bar screen, two aeration basins, four clarifiers, three filters, a tertiary chlorine contact basin, a tertiary effluent clearwell, and four Riverside Ponds that operate in series.

The tertiary wastewater treatment process prior to discharge from Discharge Point 001 includes a bar screen, two aeration basins, four clarifiers, three filters, a tertiary chlorine contact basin, a tertiary effluent clearwell, and four Riverside Ponds that operate in series.

After filtration, wastewater is routed to the tertiary chlorine contact basin. The Discharger adds sodium bisulfite in the tertiary effluent clearwell prior to routing tertiary-treated wastewater to either the Riverside Ponds or the 20-million-gallon Effluent Storage Pond.
From the Riverside Ponds, tertiary-treated wastewater is discharged via Discharge Point 001 to the Napa River.
In the future, the Riverside Ponds may be reconfigured as two ponds.
In the future, the Facility will directly discharge from this [20-million-gallon Effluent Storage] pond to Discharge Point 003.
A portion of the sludge undergoes anaerobic digestion at the El Nido Composting Facility (Central Valley Composting).

Sludge that settles to the bottom of the clarifiers is sent back to the primary distribution structure, located before the aeration basins, or to a 72,000-gallon-capacity sludge holding tank and then to the sludge drying beds.
Other upcoming Facility changes include installing a new screw press for increased sludge dewatering...
